provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after famulis tuis; 1862 sets unitatem in lower case where the 1962 capitalises Unitatem; 1862 sets no comma after ut; 1862 spells majestatis and ejusdem where the 1962 spells maiestatis and eiusdem (i/j orthography); 1862 writes the conclusion out (Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat.) where the 1962 prints the short cue Per Dominum. This is the one place in my lane where the antecedent is the longer of the two. Corroboration: not reachable. Neither the 1570 nor the 1604 scan yields the Trinity Sunday formulary to a search over its degraded text, and I will not rest a claim or a negative on such a search; the 1604 does print the votive Mass of the Holy Trinity, but its Oratio there is a different prayer. Recorded limitation: ONE LETTER INFERRED, NOT READ, AND CORROBORATED ONLY INSIDE THE SAME WITNESS. The 1862 text layer at line 47389 reads 'confessi6ne vera fidei', dropping the second element of the ae ligature. I did not repair it silently. The reading verae is supported from within the 1862 itself: the same phrase is recognised as 'verae fidei' at lines 13411 and 99852 and as 'verse fidei' at lines 60993, 92825 and 103272, so the book sets veræ and this one occurrence lost a letter to the scan. Note that 'in confessione vera' is also grammatical Latin, so this is a real inference and not a typo I can wave away, which is why confidence is medium. The 1862 also has 'Mnrpotens' at line 47387 for the ornamental O of Omnipotens. The 1862 reading rests on the text layer alone, and I could reach no page image of it.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui dedisti famulis tuis, in confessione verae
fidei, aeternae Trinitatis gloriam agnoscere, et in potentia majestatis
adorare Unitatem: quaesumus; ut, ejusdem fidei firmitate, ab omnibus semper
muniamur adversis. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
